## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Although several secondary literature sources discuss texts or authors associated with the name Upasena, they refer either to the ancient Pali commentator Upasena (author of the *Saddhammapajjotikā*) or to the discourse on snakebite preserved in the *Saḷāyatanasaṁyutta* (SN 35.69) and its Sanskrit and Chinese parallels, rather than Ud 4.9.

Parallels to the verse material of the sutta are preserved widely across early Buddhist canonical collections. Curated parallels identify corresponding verses in the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 16, Prakīrṇakavarga, and UV 32, Bhikṣuvarga), along with their Tibetan (Uv Kg 16 and 32) and Chinese witnesses (T 212.33 and T 213.32). Within the Pali canon, parallel verses are found in the *Dvayatānupassanā Sutta* (Snp 3.12) of the *Sutta Nipāta*, and the text is cited in the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 1). Computational analysis via DharmaNexus demonstrates Pali-internal text reuse with nine other canonical and post-canonical works, showing the highest volume of shared segments with the *Māra Saṁyutta* (SN 4), the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Aṭṭhakanipāta* (AN 8), the *Ghaṭikāra Sutta* (MN 81), the Vinaya *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Pārājika 1), and the *Mahākhandhaka* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignment additionally links phrasing in the text to a section of the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99, fascicle 39) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
